Cusco · Perú

Checacupe Colonial Bridge

A masonry arch beside other river crossings

Current ratingsOpening hoursView the place on the map
Nearby places

Explore

The old arched bridge is part of a river crossing where structures from different periods can be compared. Identify the masonry arch first; the neighbouring crossings have different materials and construction histories. A side view makes those differences legible.

Planning your visit

20–40 min · Allow this time for the visit itself. Add travel, admission queues and any scheduled tour separately.

What to look for

A masonry arch beside other river crossings

From the approved riverbank path, photograph the stone arch with water visible beneath. The curved profile is much harder to see when standing on the bridge deck.

History and local experience

Stand back until the abutments as well as the arch are visible. They explain how a masonry crossing meets the riverbanks and why a photograph taken on the deck tells only half the story.

Walking route

  1. Puente colonial de Checacupe, Canchis
  2. From the town approach use the indicated visitor path to the colonial bridge, stop on the bank for the arch profile and cross only where local signs allow.
  3. Keep working road crossings clear.
